newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Nan Ya Technology plans T$100 bln wafer projects.
newsitem.headline: Nan Ya Technology plans T$100 bln wafer projects.

text.p: Taiwan semiconductor maker Nan Ya Technology Corp, a subsidiary of Nan Ya Plastics, said on Monday it planned to invest more than T$100 billion in the next five years to build three wafer plants in northern Taiwan.

"We plan to build three eight-inch or 12-inch wafer plants in the next five years in (the northern) Linco town to strengthen our competitiveness," Nan Ya Plastics spokesman Wu Chia-chao told Reuters by telephone.
Nan Ya Technology will build the first wafer plant by the end of 1997, with completion seen in mid-1999, Wu said.
"We will follow suit to build the other two plants, but details have yet to be fully set," he said.

Nan Ya Technology, which was founded in 1994 to build a US$675 million dynamic random access memory chip plant, is fully owned by Formosa Plastics Group, with Nan Ya Plastics as key investor with a 56 percent stake.
Wu declined to say whether the firm's new plants will continue to focus on making DRAMs or may transfer to other chip production.

The announcement was the fifth involving major wafermaking plants in as many months, coming fast on the heels of project announcements by Taiwan's number one and two chipmakers, Taiwan Semiconductor and United Microelectronics.
In April, Taiwan Semiconductor said it was launching a T$400 billion (US$14 billion), 10-year wafer fab project.
In June, United Microelectronics announced a T$500 billion (US$18 billion), 10-year wafer fabrication project -- Taiwan's single biggest investment scheme to date.
In late June, chipmaker Winbond Electronics said it was considering huge wafer projects in a 10-year span with investment likely totalling around T$160 billion.
On July 2, TI-Acer, a joint venture of Acer Inc of Taiwan and Texas Instruments Inc, said it would invest T$100 billion to build an eight-inch wafer fabrication plant in Taiwan by 2000.
